summary: M3: WinUI 3 desktop UI plus an elevated broker. Three programs: Purge.exe (UI, medium), purge-engine --stdio (medium, read-only plus the medium-route uninstaller), purge-broker.exe (elevated, a new binary, the only release binary that links purge-exec). Every uninstall asks for UAC once; the broker harvests, scans and plans by itself; only ids cross the pipe; the broker shows the consent in its own TaskDialog and runs the plan object the dialog was drawn from. The broker is the pipe server and each side checks the other. The broker reads no directory from the environment and runs only from an admin-only directory on the system volume. Nine mockup pages are built; the UI starts from the stopgap tree at 0d9c008. Design text: docs/M3_DESIGN.md. 33 packages, 8 waves, 3 Fable review points.
starts_after: M1b gate; M3 code that does not touch the baseline may start before BL-GATE; the M3 gate runs after BL-GATE
model_routing: critical: Fable medium, or Opus high with a Fable review; high: Opus high; medium: Opus medium; trivial: Sonnet; VM campaigns: scripts under a Haiku babysitter, judged in review.
invariants: B1 Ids only: no broker request has a field for a path, target, fingerprint, scan or plan; unknown fields are refused.
B2 Own evidence: the broker executes only plans it built from its own harvest and scan; nothing made at medium integrity is evidence (BL-R1 N5, N6).
B3 One plan object: the consent dialog and the executor use the same frozen in-memory BoundPlan; nothing is derived a second time.

B4 Every request that changes something outside Purge's store ends in a TaskDialog shown by the broker; a declined dialog changes nothing. A request that writes only Purge's own records (the harvest's fingerprint, a recovery with nothing to change on the machine) runs without one (review M3-R2 point 2).
B5 Executor containment: purge-exec is linked by purge-broker, and by purge-engine only with rig-exec; purge-broker has no cargo feature.
B6 No directory from the environment in an elevated process; the broker runs only from an admin-only directory on the system volume (BL-R1 S4).
B7 Purge is never an elevation vehicle: a per-user or user-writable uninstaller runs at the user's level, in the medium engine.
B8 The broker serves one client: verified pid, creation time, image path and account.
B9 No privilege is enabled except SeRestorePrivilege on one thread around undo's owner restore.
B10 Report only: M3 closes, stops, restarts and schedules nothing; no delete without quarantine at clean time.
B11 No broker and no UAC at launch.
budgets: First Rendering tick, full S1 skeleton: at most the bare-WinUI control + 60 ms p50 in the same run; absolute guard 360 ms p50, 420 ms p90 (re-based by M3-BENCH if the host differs).
Names visible (presented frame with rows), primary gate: 400 ms p50, 460 ms p90.
Icons visible with a warm icon cache: 1 s.
First launch after install, Defender on: 1.2 s p50 over 5 fresh copies. Cold after reboot: 1.0 s p50, N >= 5.
Harvest complete after the UAC click (VS Code): 3 s. Post-uninstall scan, cold broker: 10 s, first progress within 100 ms.
Pipe line limits: 4 MiB into the broker, 64 KiB into the stdio engine, 16 MiB out. Write timeout 30 s. Idle exit 10 min.

review_points.attack: Reach an Execute method over stdio. Get a path or a document into a broker request. Start the broker from a user-writable place, another volume or with planted directories. Connect as a second client or serve a fake pipe. Keep the privilege on after its scope. Break check-deps with a feature or a dev-dependency.

Make the executor run something the dialog did not show. Run a plan of another scan, or run one twice. Get a medium-route program run by the broker. Mislead with names or paths in the dialog. Lose or corrupt a session by killing the UI at each step. Purge a user-data item without its own dialog.
The UI side of the boundary: the launcher, the server check, what the UI shows when the broker lies or dies. Can each rig mode fail (controls)? Is the e2e comparison honest? Gate readiness.

gate_procedure: Per-wave code gate (host, no VM): xtask ci, elevated and unelevated (PurgeCiUnelev); from wave 3 on with --require-ui. Each critical package gets a Fable review before its wave merges. VM gate (after BL-GATE): install on both VMs; m3-broker (G3, G10); m3-consent plus the manual SendInput test with UAC on (G4); m3-uac (G5); m3-e2e on seven apps (G6, G7, G12); m3-owner (G8); m3-recover and the purge rows (G9); m3-clean-start (G11). Host: bench-launch, first launch, cold after reboot (G2).
